08:42 Mira: The new lamps are in the stockroom. Could you put the green one in the front window before we open?
08:43 Dario: I can. The price cards that came with the lamps show the price for a set of two.
08:44 Mira: We're selling them individually until the weekend. Use a blank card for now. The unit price is on the stock sheet.
08:46 Dario: Got it. I'll leave the printed cards in the left drawer under the register.
08:47 Mira: Thanks. Leave the window light off until I get there. I want to see how the lamp looks in daylight first.

questions.question_text: Why does Mira first contact Dario?

options.text: To ask him to set up part of a display
To report a fault with a light

questions.question_text: Where is Dario told to find the price of one lamp?
What will the shop most likely be able to reuse over the weekend?

options.text: The handwritten cards for individual lamps
The printed cards that show the set price
The labels from the stockroom shelves
The tags attached to the window lights

questions.question_text: What does Mira want to assess in person?

options.text: Whether the window light needs a new bulb
How clearly the printed price can be read
How the lamp appears under natural light

From: Orla, Brindlebank Garden Centre
To: Henning Voss
Subject: The two planters on order 468

Dear Mr. Voss,

Thank you for sending a photo of the broken planter. [1] I have set aside a replacement in the same finish. [2] Please bring that tag to the service counter when you collect the replacement. A photo of the tag is fine if it is hard to remove. [3]

Our delivery van will be in your area on Friday. [4] If you would rather wait for the van, reply by Thursday at noon and I will add the replacement to its route at no charge. We can leave the replacement by your garage as we did with the original order.

questions.question_text: Why did Orla write the e-mail?

options.text: To confirm payment for two planters
To explain how a damaged item can be replaced
To ask a customer to photograph a new product
To explain a change to a delivery charge

questions.question_text: In which position marked [1], [2], [3], or [4] does the following sentence best belong? “Before we can release it, our service team will need the batch number printed on the small tag attached to the damaged planter.”
The word “finish” in the first paragraph is closest in meaning to
What should Mr. Voss do to have the planter delivered on Friday?

options.text: Call the driver on Friday morning
Bring the tag to the service counter first
Pay the delivery fee by Thursday
Reply no later than Thursday at noon

groups.passage:
**A quieter booth at Vellin Voiceworks**

When voice performers arrived at Vellin Voiceworks last autumn, they sometimes had to stop mid-sentence while the air conditioner started up. The studio considered replacing the unit, but the owner, Suki Han, discovered that the sound entered mainly through a vent directly above the microphone. She had the opening moved to the rear wall and fitted it with a lined cover. The same air conditioner now runs during recordings.

Han had initially set aside enough money for a new unit. She used part of that budget to build a second editing station after the vent work came in under budget. The extra station is reserved for short corrections on projects the studio has already recorded. Full editing jobs still go through the original workstation.

questions.question_text: What did Suki Han have moved?

options.text: An opening for air to pass through

questions.question_text: The phrase “set aside” in the second paragraph is closest in meaning to
Why was Han able to pay for the additional editing station from the same budget?

options.text: The studio stopped using the original workstation.
The old air conditioner was sold to another business.
Performers agreed to pay for short corrections.
The noise issue was resolved at less than the amount budgeted.

questions.question_text: Which job would be assigned to the second editing station?

options.text: Editing an entire interview recorded at Vellin
Recording a performer's first reading of a new script
Replacing one line in a recording made at Vellin
Preparing a complete edit of a new radio advertisement

**Nerrow Linen Supply | Trade quotation 771**
Valid through 14 August

| Product | Price per set |
| --- | --- |
| White guest-room towel set | $18 |
| Stone guest-room towel set | $20 |
| White spa towel set | $24 |

Dispatch within two working days of confirmation. Delivery is $30 per shipment for fewer than 15 sets. Shipments of 15 or more sets travel free. Please specify if the order must arrive in separate shipments.

---

From: Ines Carden, Reception Manager, Sablecourt Hotel
To: Nerrow Linen Supply
Date: 12 August
Subject: Quotation 771

Please proceed with 12 white guest-room sets and six white spa sets. We are opening a renovated guest floor on Monday and need the guest-room sets sent as soon as possible. Send the spa sets separately no earlier than the following Wednesday, when the spa storeroom will be accessible again. Please send a single invoice covering both dispatches to me. Delivery staff should use the loading entrance off Pell Street for both shipments.

questions.question_text: Why does the hotel need the guest-room sets promptly?

options.text: It needs to inspect the sets before August 14.
It is about to reopen a floor.
Its main storeroom is about to close.
It expects a shipment from the spa on Monday.

questions.question_text: How much will delivery cost in total under the quoted terms?
What will become possible on Wednesday?

options.text: Confirming the trade quotation for the first time

questions.question_text: What is the price of the ordered guest-room sets before delivery?
What does Ines request for billing?

options.text: As one invoice for the full order
As a separate invoice for each shipment
As a revised quotation valid through Wednesday
As a paper invoice carried by the first driver
